While I've only just started (less than 4 hours of play time) I have to say that playing the game on its hardest difficulty has been an immensely rewarding experience.

I've tried harder difficulties on the previous two Witches, and games like Skyrim, but the difficulty just felt like insanely inflated numbers for the enemies (health / damage dealt) and insanely reduced for me (health / damage received). In the Witcher 3, the moves at my disposal really quell that feeling of artificially increased difficulty.

The ability to dodge versus roll versus parry really opens up how you defend against attacks where in older games you just had to run from multiple enemies or hope their attacks would miss. The first fight against the ghouls took me a good 15 minutes to beat during which I learned that being surrounded meant death and that signs were not nice bonuses (as it felt in W1/2) but necessary battlefield altering techniques.

Is / has anyone else been playing on Death March? Do you feel the same or do you find it just as grindy as other games' hardest difficulties?
